newsitem.title: USA: USDA Farm Service Agency chief resigns.
newsitem.headline: USDA Farm Service Agency chief resigns.

text.p: U.S. Department of Agriculture Farm Service Agency chief Grant Buntrock has resigned effective April 4, according to a letter obtained by Reuters.
"Now, it is, quite simply, time to move on as the Clinton Administration begins a new term with a new team," Buntrock wrote in a letter to Farm Service Agency employees dated January 21.

Buntrock was administrator of USDA's Farm Service Agency for three years. The agency is in charge of USDA's domestic farm programs, including price support programs, conservation and environmental programs and farm credit programs.
Buntrock also said he was stepping down from his post as executive vice president of USDA's Commodity Credit Corp. He did not say in the letter what his next step would be.
